deep.reconstruction:
Context (prev. page). Riemann defines the Euler-type integral S(a,b,c,x)=∫_0^1 y^a(1-y)^b(1-xy)^c dy. The exponents α,β,γ,δ satisfy α+β+γ+δ=-2. Modern form: S(a,b,c,x)=Γ(a+1)Γ(b+1)/Γ(a+b+2)·2F1(-c,a+1;a+b+2;x). Riemann writes Π(s)=Γ(s+1). The page expands the connection relation at x=0 / x=1 in powers of x. He first treats the general case and then the degenerate (logarithmic) case.

(1) Connection formula, restated from p.15:
S(α,δ,γ,1-x) sin(δ+γ)π = S(α,β,γ,x) sinβπ − S(δ,γ,β,x) x^{δ+γ+1} sinγπ, with α+β+γ+δ=-2.
This is Gauss's/Kummer's 1−x ↔ x connection formula for 2F1 in Riemann's integral normalisation. Here a=-γ, b=α+1, c=α+δ+2, so c−a−b=δ+γ+1 and a+b−c+1=α+β+2.

(2) Series of the first right-hand term:
S(α,β,γ,x) = Σ_n Π(n−1−γ)Π(n+α)/(Πn Π(n+α+β+1)) x^n · Πβ/Π(−1−γ).
This holds since (−γ)_n=Π(n−1−γ)/Π(−1−γ), (α+1)_n=Π(n+α)/Πα and (α+β+2)_n=Π(n+α+β+1)/Π(α+β+1). On the page he multiplies by sinβπ.

(3) Reflection (Euler): Πβ Π(−1−β) = −π/sinβπ, so Πβ sinβπ/Π(−1−γ) = −π/(Π(−1−β)Π(−1−γ)). The same holds with β↔γ. These are written again as scratch at the bottom of the page.

(4) Both terms on the right then carry the same constant −π/(Π(−1−β)Π(−1−γ)). The second term is the analogous series with (α,β,γ)→(δ,γ,β). This gives:
S(α,δ,γ,1−x) sin(δ+γ)π = −π/(Π(−1−β)Π(−1−γ)) · [ Σ_{n≥0} Π(n−1−γ)Π(n+α)/(Πn Π(n+α+β+1)) x^n − Σ_{n≥0} Π(n−1−β)Π(n+δ)/(Πn Π(n+γ+δ+1)) x^{n+γ+δ+1} ].
He writes this once with the constant moved to the left and once to the right, then recopies the connection formula.

(5) Degenerate case: α+β+1=m, δ+γ+1=−m, m a positive integer. Both sin(δ+γ)π and the two series become singular. Passing to the limit (the limit step is implicit) gives:
S(α,δ,γ,1−x) Π(α−m) Π(δ+m) (−1)^{m−1}
 = Σ_{n=−m}^{−1} (−1)^{n−1} Π(n+α)Π(n+m+δ)Π(−n−1)/Π(n+m) x^n
 + Σ_{n=0}^{∞} Π(n+α)Π(n+m+δ)/(Πn Π(n+m)) x^n [ψ(n+α)+ψ(n+m+δ)−ψ(n)−ψ(n+m)+log x],
with ψ(s)=d log Π(s)/ds = digamma(s+1).
In the finite sum the factor Π(−n−1) with sign (−1)^{n−1} is written over or partly struck. My derivation shows (−1)^{n+1}Π(−n−1) is required.

Check (mine): with a=−γ=δ+1+m, b=α+1, c=a+b−m, the formula A&S 15.3.12 times B(α+1,δ+1) gives exactly this. Note Γ(δ+1)/Γ(−γ−m)=1.
- Log part: −(−1)^m/(Π(α−m)Π(δ+m)) · Π(n+α)Π(n+m+δ)/(n!(n+m)!) [log x − ψ(n+1) − ψ(n+m+1) + ψ(n+α+1) + ψ(n+m+δ+1)].
- Finite part: (−1)^k Π(δ+k)Π(α−m+k)(m−1−k)!/(Π(δ+m)Π(α−m)k!) x^{k−m}, which becomes (−1)^{n+1}Π(n+α)Π(n+m+δ)Π(−n−1)/Π(n+m) x^n with n=k−m.

(6) Two struck lines, S(−β−1,−α−1,−δ−1,x) and S(α−m,β−m,γ+m,x). Under α+β+1=m, δ+γ+1=−m these are identical: −β−1=α−m, −α−1=β−m, −δ−1=γ+m. This is an aborted attempt to rewrite a term via the parameters shifted by m.
errors: Line 4 apparently writes the integrand factor as (1−xy)^δ. It must be (1−xy)^γ, as in the definition two lines above. This is a slip.
Line 4 ends with ·sinβπ on the right while the left side is S(α,β,γ,x) alone. The intended statement is S(α,β,γ,x)·sinβπ = Σ… · Πβ sinβπ/Π(−1−γ).
In the degenerate formula the finite-sum coefficient needs the factor (−1)^{n−1}Π(−n−1). On the page this factor is written over or partly struck; without it the formula is wrong.
The passage to the limit in the degenerate case (cancelling the poles of the two series against sin(δ+γ)π → 0) is not written out. Only the result is given, but the result is correct.
Otherwise all steps check: the connection formula, the series coefficients and the reflection identities are correct.

results.what: Connection formula S(α,δ,γ,1−x)sin(δ+γ)π = S(α,β,γ,x)sinβπ − S(δ,γ,β,x)x^{δ+γ+1}sinγπ (α+β+γ+δ=−2), with explicit power series about x=0
results.modern_name: Gauss/Kummer connection formula 2F1(a,b;c;1−x) in terms of solutions at x=0 (DLMF 15.10.21 / A&S 15.3.6)

results.what: Gamma reflection Π(β)Π(−1−β) = −π/sin βπ used to normalize coefficients
Logarithmic expansion of S(α,δ,γ,1−x) about x=0 when α+β+1=m, δ+γ+1=−m (integer exponent difference): finite Laurent part plus series with digamma terms and log x
results.modern_name: Degenerate (logarithmic) case of the 2F1 connection formula, A&S 15.3.12 / DLMF 15.8.10
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Kummer (1836) for log cases; explicit digamma form standard in later literature (e.g. Bateman/Erdélyi)

deep.surprise_reason: These are correct working computations in Riemann's 1857 P-function framework. The connection formula and its series are classical (Gauss, Kummer), and Riemann's 1857 paper notes logarithmic cases. The explicit, correct digamma/log expansion for an integer exponent difference is a nice unpublished detail, but it was already essentially known (Kummer) and is standard.

transcription_corrections: Line 4: the integrand should read (1−xy)^γ; the machine reading (1−xy)^δ either misreads the image or reproduces a slip by Riemann.

The finite-sum coefficient in the degenerate formula is Π(n+α)Π(n+m+δ)·Π(−n−1)·(−1)^{n−1}/Π(n+m). The overwritten exponent is n−1 (the sign); the transcription wrongly treats Π(−n−1) as simply deleted.
'S(α,δ,γ_{1−m},1−x)' should be read as S(α,δ,γ,1−x), with '1−m' a marginal or subscript note (probably γ+δ+1=−m).
The two struck lines S(−β−1,−α−1,−δ−1,x) and S(α−m,β−m,γ+m,x) are equal under the stated conditions; the first is a cancelled attempt, not a separate result.
Riemann's ψ denotes d/ds log Π(s) = digamma(s+1), not digamma(s).
